controls.label: Shape
controls.qualification: A sphere of the published radius, lit by GJ 1132; the neutral gray is a display convention, not a measured color.
controls.notes: No image or color of GJ 1132 b is published: the sphere has its measured size, and the gray marks an unresolved surface. The lighting is its own star's, at the measured orbit. The gray takes the color of gj-1132's light, as its color dataset measures it.

charts.alt: The orbits of GJ 1132's planets in this map from above, to scale, with GJ 1132 b highlighted and the direction to Earth down. Each orbit is the one the app draws, from the published period, a/R*, eccentricity and argument of periastron; the star is a marker, not to scale.

GJ 1132 b's transmission spectrum: the fraction of starlight the planet blocks as it crosses its star, larger where its atmosphere absorbs. 17 measured bins from Diamond-Lowe et al. 2018 (Magellan II Landon Clay Telescope, LDSS-3C), as the NASA Exoplanet Archive lists them. Horizontal bars are wavelength bins; vertical bars are the published 1-sigma errors.

GJ 1132 b crossing its star, as TESS recorded it: 3 sectors (63, 90, 99) of the SPOC pipeline's 2-minute light curves of TIC 101955023, each transit divided by a straight line fitted to the light either side and folded onto the orbit the app draws, then averaged in 4-minute bins. Error bars are each bin's standard error.

physical.credit: Radius from Xue et al. 2024 (2024ApJ...973L...8X), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive; mass from Xue et al. 2024, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2024ApJ...973L...8X), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive; orbit from Xue et al. 2024 (2024ApJ...973L...8X), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive
